description: The screenshot shows a Windows desktop with three applications visible: on the left is Azure Data Studio (or similar SQL IDE) with a SQL query open that contains a SELECT statement querying from "all_tables" with conditions including table_name filtering and joins; the query results are displayed below in a tabular format with columns showing table_name, table_size, time_created, and other metadata with rows highlighted in yellow. In the center is a dark-themed web browser (likely Edge based on the URL bar showing "https://s365.blob4.microsoft...." with an Azure/Microsoft 365 interface showing a list of items dated January 2026 with an "API LLM Test" panel on the right side. The taskbar at the bottom shows various pinned applications including File Explorer, and the system tray indicates it's 9:51 AM with network and other status icons visible.

The screen shows a split view with DBeaver database IDE on the left displaying SQL code with queries against tables including `a_table_name`, `all_tables`, and operations involving `left join`, `group by`, and `select` statements. The query results panel below shows a table with columns including `TABLE_NAME`, `TABLE_ROWS`, and `AVG_ROW_LENGTH` with multiple rows of highlighted (yellow) data. On the right side is a Microsoft browser window showing what appears to be an Azure or Microsoft admin portal with a dark interface containing a task list or notification panel titled "Tasks to Run in January 2025" with multiple items including tasks related to "Copilot" integration, data handling, and various system maintenance items. The Windows 11 taskbar is visible at the bottom showing the time as 9:31 AM.

The screen shows a split view with DBeaver database IDE on the left side, displaying a SQL query editor with highlighted SQL code (SELECT statements with joins on tables including `table_name`, `table_size`, `table_sizep`, `time_created` columns) and a results grid below showing timestamped database entries with yellow-highlighted rows from dates around 2020-01-12. On the right side, there appears to be a Microsoft Azure Data Explorer (Kusto) web interface in a dark-themed browser window, showing a query panel with "Stories to Run in January 2020" visible in the header, along with a list of items/queries and a results panel showing what appears to be log or event data with various metadata columns. The user appears to be working with database queries across two different tools, likely comparing or transferring data between DBeaver and Azure Data Explorer.

The screen shows a split view with DBeaver (database IDE) on the left displaying a SQL query against "m.table_name" with yellow highlighted syntax for a SELECT statement querying table metadata including fields like "table_size, table_rows, table_name, time_created". On the right side is a Brave browser window showing the Claude AI chat interface (claude.ai) in dark mode, with a conversation visible containing text about "What to run now (Jan 2026): practical rule" and several collapsed response sections including topics about file formats and practical recommendations. The Windows taskbar is visible at the bottom showing various pinned applications including Visual Studio Code and other development tools.

The screen shows a split-panel development environment with VS Code on the left displaying a Python script (containing SQL queries with highlighted yellow lines showing table_name, table_rows, table_size operations and references to "env_all_tables" and database schema functions), and a Firefox browser on the right showing a Claude AI chat interface. The VS Code panel also shows a data table/spreadsheet below the code with numbered rows (1-25 visible) containing what appears to be database table listings. The user appears to be reading or referencing the Claude conversation while working on a database-related Python script, with the waybar at the bottom showing the date "Jan 16" and various system tray icons.
